name: Skincare 'skin cycling'
summary: TikTok-famous four-night rotation of exfoliant, retinoid and two recovery nights; reasonable by derm convention but never trialled.
lead: Skin cycling is a rotating skincare routine that alternates nights of exfoliant and retinoid use with nights of recovery. According to Grokipedia, it was created by New York dermatologist Whitney Bowe, introduced in April 2021, and went viral on TikTok in 2022 .

name: Oral antibiotics (doxycycline/minocycline)
summary: Prescription tetracyclines for inflammatory acne; established in dermatology, with documented side effects and resistance concerns.
lead: Doxycycline and minocycline are tetracycline-class antibiotics that dermatologists prescribe for inflammatory acne and rosacea. Both are prescription-only in the US and other countries .
claims: Antibiotics destroy gut flora and should be avoided unless truly needed

name: Topical clindamycin
summary: Rx antibiotic gel or lotion for mild to moderate acne, usually paired with benzoyl peroxide; well studied, with resistance a recognised concern.
lead: Topical clindamycin is a prescription antibiotic lotion, gel or foam used for mild to moderate acne, often combined with benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid. It is a semisynthetic derivative of lincomycin, announced in 1966 and marketed since 1968 .

name: Dapsone gel (Aczone)
summary: Rx anti-inflammatory gel for acne with large phase 3 trial programs; usually mild irritation.
lead: Dapsone gel, sold as Aczone, is a prescription topical gel for acne vulgaris. Wikipedia reports that QLT USA developed the 5% gel in the early 2000s and that the FDA approved a 7.5% gel in February 2016 .

name: Sarecycline (Seysara)
summary: A once-daily, narrow-spectrum oral tetracycline approved in 2018 for inflammatory acne; a prescription antibiotic, not a looksmaxxing staple.
lead: Sarecycline, sold in the United States under the brand name Seysara, is an oral tetracycline-class antibiotic approved for acne vulgaris. The FDA approved the tablet formulation in early October 2018 for the treatment of inflammatory lesions of non-nodular moderate to severe acne in patients aged 9 years and older .

name: Combined oral contraceptive pill
summary: The estrogen-plus-progestin birth control pill, also prescribed for hormonal acne in women because it lowers free androgens.
lead: The combined oral contraceptive pill (COC) is a hormonal medicine containing an estrogen and a progestin, taken mainly for contraception. It is also prescribed for acne and hirsutism in women, since lowering androgen activity reduces sebum production .

name: Low-dose isotretinoin (microdosing Accutane)
summary: Using small continuous isotretinoin (Accutane) amounts, instead of a standard course, to keep acne away with fewer side effects; discussed online, thinly documented here.
lead: Low-dose isotretinoin, popularly called microdosing Accutane, is the practice of taking markedly smaller doses of isotretinoin than the standard acne regimen, in some cases as an ongoing maintenance approach. Isotretinoin is a prescription retinoid first patented by Roche in 1969 and approved by the FDA in 1982 .
claims: A tiny maintenance amount after a full course keeps acne from coming back
A low-dose oral retinoid and a low-strength topical retinoid can be used together

name: Spearmint tea
summary: A herbal tea said to lower androgens and calm hormonal acne; one small trial studied androgens in PCOS, and none tested acne.
lead: Spearmint tea is made by steeping the leaves of spearmint (Mentha spicata), a perennial herb native to Europe and southern temperate Asia that is widely used as a flavouring and in teas such as Maghrebi mint tea .

name: Low-glycemic diet for acne
summary: Eating low-GI carbs to calm acne: the one diet tweak with some trial support, though the evidence is modest.
lead: A low-glycemic diet (low-GI or low-glycemic-load diet) is an eating pattern built around foods that raise blood glucose slowly, used by some people with acne in the hope of reducing breakouts. The glycemic index, introduced by David Jenkins and colleagues in 1981, ranks carbohydrate foods from 0 to 100 against pure glucose, and glycemic load adjusts that ranking for portion size.

name: Fungal acne protocol (Malassezia)
summary: Avoiding fatty-acid oils and using antifungals for itchy forehead and body bumps attributed to Malassezia yeast, a recognised condition called Malassezia folliculitis.
lead: Fungal acne is a popular name for Malassezia folliculitis, also called pityrosporum folliculitis. It is a skin condition in which yeast of the genus Malassezia, a normal part of human skin flora, overgrows within hair follicles and produces itchy papules and pustules . Despite the name it is not acne vulgaris, which involves different processes.
claims: Stubborn forehead bumps that do not respond to normal acne care are fungal acne
Fatty-acid oils in products feed the yeast and should be avoided

name: Double cleansing
summary: Oil cleanser first, foam cleanser second; a popular nightly routine that no trial has actually tested.
lead: Double cleansing is a two-step facial washing routine in which an oil-based or other lipid-soluble cleanser (a cleansing oil, balm or micellar water) is applied first, followed by a water-based cleanser that is emulsified with water and rinsed off. It is associated with Korean and Japanese beauty routines and is described in looksmaxxing and skincare communities as an evening step used to remove sunscreen, makeup and sebum.
claims: Cleansing twice, oil first, removes sunscreen and sebum that one wash leaves behind.
Double cleansing keeps pores clear and helps acne-prone skin.

name: Skin cycling
summary: A four-night rotation of acid, retinoid and two rest nights; popular and plausible, but the schedule itself has never been trialled.
lead: Skin cycling is a skincare routine that rotates evenings of active ingredients with evenings of recovery. It was introduced in April 2021 by New York dermatologist Whitney Bowe and spread widely on TikTok in 2022.
claims: Alternating actives with rest nights gives retinoid results with less irritation.
Skin cycling suits sensitive, acne-prone or barrier-damaged skin.

name: Oil cleansing method
summary: Massage oil in to dissolve sebum and makeup; popular and divisive for acne, with no trials of the method itself.
lead: The oil cleansing method is a facial cleansing practice in which a plant oil, or blend of oils, is massaged into dry skin to dissolve makeup, sunscreen and sebum, then emulsified with water and rinsed or wiped off. Common blends pair a thicker oil such as castor oil with a lighter carrier oil, and it is frequently used as the first step of a double cleanse.
claims: Oil dissolves sebum and clogged pores better than foaming cleansers.

name: Chemical peels for acne
summary: Salicylic, glycolic or Jessner peels for acne; small studies exist, but guidance calls evidence insufficient to recommend them.
lead: A chemical peel is a treatment, most often applied to the face, in which a chemical agent removes the outer skin layers; the controlled injury causes peeling and can smooth texture and reduce acne scars and pigmentation. For acne, the agents most often discussed are salicylic acid (a beta hydroxy acid), glycolic acid (an alpha hydroxy acid), Jessner solution and trichloroacetic acid (TCA), used in a dermatology office or, at lower strengths, at home.
claims: Salicylic acid peels clear acne and control oil.
Home peels give results similar to professional ones.

name: Photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT)
summary: Photosensitizer plus light for severe acne; some trials and a review are positive, but results are mixed and treatment is painful.
lead: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) uses a light-sensitive drug (photosensitizer) and light of a suitable wavelength to produce reactive oxygen species that kill targeted cells. In ALA-PDT, aminolevulinic acid (ALA), a precursor in the body's heme synthesis, is applied so that cells accumulate the photosensitizer protoporphyrin IX before light is shone on the area.
claims: ALA-PDT can clear severe or inflammatory acne.
The procedure is painful and leaves skin red for days.

name: Professional extractions / acne facial
summary: Manual blackhead and whitehead removal by a pro; standard practice, with little formal trial evidence.
lead: Professional comedone extraction is the manual removal of blackheads and whiteheads by an esthetician or dermatologist, usually as part of an acne facial. Practitioners use comedo extractors with attention to hygiene, typically after steaming the face or washing with warm water.
claims: Professional extraction is safer than squeezing at home.

name: Intralesional cortisone injection
summary: A dermatologist-administered steroid shot into an inflamed cyst, discussed online as an overnight shrinker; evidence is not detailed in the sources reviewed.
lead: An intralesional cortisone injection is a procedure in which a clinician injects a corticosteroid directly into an inflamed lesion, such as a painful acne cyst or nodule. In appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a way to flatten a large pimple quickly, often described as shrinking a cyst "overnight".

name: Toothpaste on pimples
summary: The classic overnight dab of toothpaste on a pimple; no studies were found and toothpaste is not designed for skin.
lead: Dabbing toothpaste on a pimple overnight is a long-circulating home remedy for acne. Practitioners say it dries out the spot.

name: Apple cider vinegar toner
summary: Diluted ACV dabbed on the face as an acne toner; no studies found and burns are documented.
lead: Apple cider vinegar (ACV) toner is a diluted vinegar applied to the face as a homemade toner, which proponents use for acne and oiliness.

name: Lemon juice on pimples
summary: Lemon juice dabbed on blemishes; no studies found, and citrus-plus-sun skin reactions are documented.
lead: Dabbing lemon juice on pimples is a home remedy for acne and dark marks. Proponents cite its acidity and vitamin C.

name: Aspirin mask
summary: Crushed-aspirin face paste for acne; relies on its link to salicylic acid, with no studies found.
lead: An aspirin mask is a home paste made by crushing aspirin tablets, applied to the face, mainly for acne and redness. Proponents note that aspirin is related to salicylic acid, a common acne ingredient.

name: Honey mask (manuka)
summary: Manuka honey smeared on the face for acne; wound studies exist for honey, but none for acne were found.
lead: A manuka honey mask is honey from the mānuka tree applied to the face, used by proponents for acne and skin calming.

name: Bentonite / clay mask
summary: Oil-absorbing clay paste for rinse-off masks; popular for oily skin but with no clinical trials behind the cosmetic claims.
lead: A bentonite clay mask is a wash-off facial or body product whose main ingredient is bentonite, an absorbent clay composed mostly of the mineral montmorillonite. Such masks are marketed for soaking up skin oil and are used in skincare routines aimed at oily or congested skin .

name: Vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid) high dose
summary: Megadose B5 pitched for oil control; no acne trials found, though no upper intake limit exists.
lead: Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a water-soluble vitamin that animals need to make coenzyme A, which is involved in energy metabolism and fatty acid synthesis . In looksmaxxing and skincare circles, very high supplemental intakes are discussed as a way to reduce skin oil and acne.

name: Probiotics for acne
summary: Gut-skin axis supplements and creams for acne; reviews and trials exist, but evidence is preliminary and strain-specific.
lead: Probiotics are live microorganisms intended to confer a health benefit, sold as supplements, in fermented foods and in some topical products . For acne, oral and topical probiotics are discussed on the basis of the proposed gut-skin axis and of the skin's own microbial community .

name: DIM supplement
summary: Broccoli-derived estrogen-metabolism supplement used for hormonal acne; the research is on cancer and hormones, not skin.
lead: 3,3'-Diindolylmethane (DIM) is a compound formed when the body digests indole-3-carbinol, which occurs in cruciferous vegetables such as broccoli, cabbage and Brussels sprouts. It is sold as a dietary supplement .

name: Hypochlorous acid spray
summary: Mist version of a chemical your white blood cells make; established in wound and eyelid care, untested for looks.
lead: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) spray is a mist containing a dilute solution of hypochlorous acid, a weak acid that forms when chlorine dissolves in water. It is marketed as a skin-safe antimicrobial for face and body care .

name: Accure laser (1726 nm)
summary: 1726 nm laser aimed at oil glands for acne; registered trials exist but published results were not found here.
lead: Accure is a laser procedure that targets sebaceous (oil) glands with a 1726 nm wavelength as a treatment for acne. It belongs to the same class of selective sebaceous-gland lasers as Aviclear .

name: Isolaz / pulsed light acne treatment
summary: Vacuum plus pulsed light for clogged pores; a clinic add-on with thin public evidence behind it.
lead: Isolaz is a brand of in-office device that combines suction (vacuum) applied to the skin with pulses of broad-spectrum light, marketed for clogged pores and acne. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed under the broader heading of pulsed-light treatments for acne-prone skin.

name: Sun exposure for acne
summary: Tanning to dry out spots; reference sources link sun to lingering dark marks rather than clearer skin.
lead: Sun exposure for acne is the practice of tanning or sitting in sunlight in the belief that it dries out blemishes. Community members sometimes report a short-term improvement in appearance.
